text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand your condition, can you describe the nature of your chest pain and when the vomiting started?

speaker: Patient
text: 51-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with persistent, forceful vomiting after consuming a significant amount of alcohol. His medical history includes recent treatment for Lyme disease with doxycycline. Recently, after a prolonged episode of retching, the patient starts to choke and cough forcefully, experiencing chest pain. The patient appears unable to communicate effectively at this point.

speaker: Doctor
text:
REQUEST TEST: Chest_CT_Scan
REQUEST TEST: Esophagogram_with_contrast

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Chest_CT_Scan: Pneumomediastinum present with extraluminal air and fluid collection in the posterior mediastinum, consistent with esophageal perforation. Esophagogram_with_contrast: Extravasation of contrast material from the distal esophagus into the mediastinum, confirming full-thickness esophageal tear.

speaker: Doctor
text: The imaging confirms a full-thickness esophageal tear with mediastinal leakage, which is diagnostic of Boerhaave syndrome. DIAGNOSIS READY: Boerhaave syndrome
